annotations.description: 1.02 checkpoint(s) failed in the last 10 minutes.

diagnosis.summary: Flink checkpoint failures are caused by a task manager restart ~2 minutes ago (exit code 255); the job is now RUNNING/STABLE and completing ~25 checkpoints per 5 min. Root disruption traces back to a chaos-mesh experiment deployed ~144 min ago that force-killed all Kafka brokers and the Flink job simultaneously.
diagnosis.root_cause: A chaos-mesh-local deployment ~144 minutes ago (revision 9187ff9e9e6f) triggered a platform-wide fault: all three Kafka brokers and the Flink jobmanager were terminated with exit code 255 (Unknown) at approximately the same time (~140.9 min ago). The Flink job recovered and ran stably for ~139 minutes, but a final task manager restart occurred ~1.9 minutes ago ('The TaskExecutor is shutting down' event), which interrupted in-flight checkpoints and pushed failed_checkpoints_last_10m to 2.1 — crossing the alert threshold. With the task manager back up, the job is now checkpointing successfully (~25 completed in the last 5 min, 0 backpressure) and should clear the alert as the failure window ages out.
diagnosis.impact: No data loss expected (exactly-once semantics, job restarted from latest checkpoint). Consumer lag is 650 offsets — small and draining. Data visibility in Iceberg lakehouse.events was delayed during the disruption (~2 min) but is now recovering. Separately, the lakehouse.events table has 146/146 small files (all files below 32 MiB), which degrades query performance until compaction runs.

evidence.finding: Job state RUNNING, lifecycle STABLE; uptime_seconds=96 (restarted ~1.6 min ago); failed_checkpoints_last_10m=2.104; completed_checkpoints_last_5m=24.995; restarts_last_15m=1.018; consumer_lag=650; task manager pod events-to-iceberg-taskmanager-2-2 age=1.9 min (brand new). Jobmanager last terminated 140.9 min ago with exit_code=255.

Warning JobException on FlinkDeployment/events-to-iceberg 1.9 min ago: 'org.apache.flink.util.FlinkExpectedException: The TaskExecutor is shutting down' — confirms task manager restart triggered the most recent checkpoint failures.

All 3 brokers Running/Ready; under_replicated_partitions=0, under_min_isr_partitions=0, offline_partitions=0, active_controllers=1. All brokers last terminated 140.9 min ago with exit_code=255 — same timestamp as Flink disruption.
chaos-mesh-local deployed revision 9187ff9e9e6f at 144.6 min ago — immediately before the mass exit_code=255 terminations at ~140.9 min ago across all Kafka brokers and Flink jobmanager.
All Argo CD applications Synced and Healthy; chaos-mesh-local is at the latest revision 47886843e767 (Succeeded). No ongoing deployment issues.
lakehouse.events: 146 data files, all 146 are small files (<32 MiB); 776 snapshots; last_commit 2 min ago (Flink is committing); last_compaction 3.8 hours ago. Compaction is overdue.
All 4 nodes Ready; no pressure conditions; no unschedulable nodes. Zone coverage intact (zone-a, zone-b, zone-c).

docs/runbooks/pipeline.md#flinkcheckpointfailures: a single failure during broker restart or node drain is expected; job tolerates 3 consecutive failures before restarting. No manual action prescribed for self-resolving failures.

proposed_action.rationale: The Flink job is RUNNING and STABLE, actively completing ~5 checkpoints per minute with zero backpressure. The 2 failed checkpoints in the 10-minute window are attributable to the task manager restart that just completed ~2 minutes ago. Per the runbook, single-event failures during disruptions are expected and the job is self-healing. Restarting the job now would be more disruptive than letting it drain the consumer lag naturally. The alert should auto-clear as the failed-checkpoint counter ages out of the 10-minute window.

follow_ups: Run Iceberg compaction on lakehouse.events immediately: all 146 data files are small files and there are 776 snapshots — query performance will be degraded until compaction runs (run_iceberg_compaction when ready).

Identify what chaos-mesh experiment was introduced at revision 9187ff9e9e6f ~144 min ago; confirm it was intentional and that the blast radius (simultaneous kill of all 3 Kafka brokers + Flink) is expected test behaviour.

Investigate why task manager pod events-to-iceberg-taskmanager-2-2 restarted ~1.9 minutes ago, separate from the original chaos event (~141 min ago) — check if a second chaos experiment was run or if the task manager OOM'd/evicted.
Monitor consumer_lag (currently 650) over the next 10–15 minutes to confirm it drains to zero; escalate if lag grows instead.
Iceberg exporter pod iceberg-exporter-57567747cd-czzt2 had readiness probe failures 27 min ago — verify it is healthy and confirm the small-file metrics are accurate.

2. All brokers had termination ~140.9 minutes ago (exit code 255, Unknown reason) - same time as the Flink job restart
3. There's consumer lag of 650 and failed_checkpoints_last_10m: 2.104

The Flink taskmanager-2-2 pod is only 1.9 minutes old - very recently restarted.
The jobmanager pod also shows 1 restart, terminated 140.9 minutes ago, though it started 139.4 minutes ago while uptime_seconds reads only 96 - that discrepancy makes sense if uptime_seconds tracks the streaming job itself rather than the pod, confirming the job just restarted. Now I want to check the nodes.

I also notice failed_checkpoints_last_10m is 2.104, higher than the 1.02 cited in the alert, so this issue seems ongoing. I'll dig into Iceberg table health, node status, and the jobmanager logs next.
Let me check the previous run of the jobmanager pod to understand why it failed, and also look at events in the apps namespace.
Let me look at the Loki logs to understand what happened when checkpoints failed. Let me also check recent changes.

Let me look at the chaos-mesh deployment from ~144 minutes ago, which is close to when the pods terminated (~140 minutes ago). There was a chaos-mesh-local deployment at 144.6 minutes ago (revision 9187ff9e9e6f), and all kafka brokers and flink job had terminations ~140.9 minutes ago.

This strongly suggests that chaos-mesh injected a fault (network partition or pod kill) that caused all brokers and the Flink job to restart around 140-141 minutes ago. This would explain checkpoint failures during the disruption.

The current status:
- Flink job: RUNNING, STABLE, but uptime_seconds = 96 (just restarted 1.6 minutes ago!)
- failed_checkpoints_last_10m still at 2.104, consumer lag at 650, and there's a TaskExecutor shutdown event 1.9 minutes ago, suggesting the job is still cycling through restarts rather than having truly stabilized. Something's off too - the job apparently started 139.4 minutes ago but shows only 96 seconds of uptime, which doesn't add up.

So it seems the pod itself has been alive for 139 minutes, but the Flink job inside it just restarted within the last 1.6 minutes - the TaskExecutor shutdown event and the taskmanager pod's 1.9 minute age both confirm this. It looks like the task manager got terminated, forcing the job to restart and retry, which is what's driving the checkpoint failures. The chaos-mesh deployment around 144 minutes ago was likely the root cause of this whole disruption cycle.

With 1 restart logged in the last 15 minutes and the job now showing RUNNING/STABLE with 96 seconds of uptime, it seems like the job just recovered from a task manager restart, but 2.104 failed checkpoints in the last 10 minutes explains why the alert is still active. I need to figure out whether this is ongoing instability from the chaos-mesh fault or if it's simply still settling after recovery, and whether a manual restart is even warranted here.

Now let me put together the full picture:

1. **~144 minutes ago**: chaos-mesh-local was deployed (revision 9187ff9e9e6f). This likely introduced a chaos experiment.

2. **~141 minutes ago**: All 3 Kafka brokers and the Flink jobmanager terminated with exit code 255 (Unknown reason) - this is consistent with a chaos-mesh fault (network partition, pod kill, etc.).

3. **~139 minutes ago**: Flink jobmanager pod restarted and has been running since.
4. About 1.9 minutes ago, the Flink task manager restarted, briefly knocking out the task executor and causing checkpoint failures that triggered the alert. Checking current state now: the job is RUNNING and STABLE with uptime around 96 seconds since that restart, and checkpoints are completing healthily at roughly 5 per minute (every ~12s).

The job is actively recovering with healthy checkpointing now, so the alert should clear once the failed checkpoint count ages out of the 10-minute window.

My proposed action is to do nothing for the checkpoint alert itself since the job is RUNNING/STABLE and checkpointing is already working, but I should flag the iceberg small-file buildup as a separate follow-up.
